newsitem.title: ITALY: Italian '97 GDP will be close to '96 levels - Fazio.
newsitem.headline: Italian '97 GDP will be close to '96 levels - Fazio.

text.p: Italian gross domestic product (GDP) in 1997 will be close to 1996 levels, well short of government targets, Bank of Italy governor Antonio Fazio said on Thursday in a speech in a speech to mark the world day of savings.
Latest government forecasts predict the economy will grow by 0.8 percent this year and 2.0 percent in 1997.
But Fazio disagreed, saying: "Economic growth in 1997 will not be far from the unsatisfactory figure seen this year."
He went on: "The modest increase seen in family income limits consumption demand, while the expansion of investments is being weighed down by a perception of uncertain development in global demand."

However he predicted that Italy would maintain its current trade surplus "for the years to come", and he was also upbeat about inflation prospects, saying consumer prices in October were unchanged month-on-month compared with September.

"Inflation should hold under three percent in the last quarter of the year," Fazio said. "The objective remains that of an average which is clearly lower than (three percent) in 1997, in line with other major industrialised countries."
Inflation in September came in at 3.4 percent year-on-year. Preliminary data for October pointed to a year-on-year figure of around 3.0 percent.
Fazio reiterated that Italy would soon become a net creditor rather than a net debitor with foreign countries.

"Together with the overhaul of public finances, this represents a indispensable requirement for consolidating the external value of the currency and for a final recovery of internal purchasing power," Fazio said.
"Monetary stability and the re-balancing of public accounts are vital if we are to exit from the current phase of economic stagnation and weakness with regard to prospects for development," he added.
Fazio said the current high levels of unemployment demanded increased investment as well as changes to labour laws.
"In the absence of this, the Italian economy is destined to grow only moderatly and will not be in a position to significantly increase the employement total," he said. -- Rome newsroom +396 6782501
